name: Merrimack River Watershed Council CSO page (per-plant sign-up guide, CSO charts)
waters_covered: Merrimack River main stem, Manchester NH to Newburyport MA
access_detail: Page fetched. No feed, no event list, no alert system of its own. It links to each plant's sign-up: Lawrence (GLSD) Everbridge https://member.everbridge.net/355009111785667/login ; Lowell https://www.lowellma.gov/1287/Combined-Sewer-Overflows-CSO ; Manchester NH https://www.manchesternh.gov/Departments/Sewer-and-Stormwater/CSO/CSO-Discharge-Notification ; Haverhill by email to ilewis@haverhillma.gov ; Nashua website only https://www.nashuanh.gov/392/Wastewater-Department
cadence: Static page; charts built from 2018-2021 data, image files dated March 2022
history: Monthly and annual CSO volume charts 2018-2021 (Manchester excluded; Haverhill 2021 missing)
legal_basis: MA Chapter 322 of the Acts of 2020 / 314 CMR 16.00 (MA plants only); NH plants under EPA orders
status_reason: The brief assumed MRWC runs a CSO alert system with texts, emails and an app. It does not: the page says there is no centralized system and sends readers to five separate plant sign-ups. Useful as a partner and as proof of the gap DirtyWaterWatch would fill, not as a feed.
notes: Page quote: plant emails 'are not always easy to understand'; advice: 'Before you visit the river for recreation, consider how long ago a CSO occurred.' Page says 'Four' plants then lists five. Lawrence data link points to the Haverhill page (site error).

name: MRWC volunteer bacteria monitoring dashboards (Merrimack main stem)
waters_covered: 13 main-stem sites Manchester NH to Newburyport/Salisbury MA
access_detail: Program page fetched. ArcGIS dashboards https://merrimackriver.maps.arcgis.com/apps/dashboards/0401c85576b44f6c93a20d4c182a5e38 and .../3d6cee5113d4435e83ef53df83419992 ; underlying feature layers not yet probed. Annual report PDF https://merrimack.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/MRWC_2024_Water_Quality_Report_for-Digital.pdf
cadence: Twice monthly spring to fall, monthly in winter; posting lag not stated
status_reason: Only regular bacteria sampling on the Merrimack main stem from one organisation; the dashboards' feature layers are probably queryable. Probe the ArcGIS org next and ask MRWC about reuse.
notes: Categorises results as 'safe' or 'unsafe' for recreation; no numeric thresholds on the page. Older report links all point to the 2024 PDF. Funded by MassBays NEP under EPA grant 00A01085-0.

name: MVPC / Merrimack River Collaborative CSO Early Alert Tool (prototype)
waters_covered: Merrimack River below Lowell to Newburyport
access_detail: Not reached. Search results say MVPC got Community Compact funding to expand a prototype CSO Early Alert Tool (created under the Merrimack River District Commission, now Merrimack River Collaborative) that predicts downstream bacteria after CSO events using time of travel and decay constants, with a GIS dashboard. Dashboard URL not found.
cadence: unknown
status_reason: The only New England attempt found to model downstream reach and duration after a CSO. Its public status is unclear (a quote in search results called it 'not ready for prime time').
notes: Follow up with MVPC: dashboard URL, whether the model and its decay constants can be shared. An accesswater.org paper 'Real-time predictive modeling for public water quality alerts' appears related.

name: Charles River Watershed Association Flagging Program (boathouse flags, website, Public Flagging API)
operator: Charles River Watershed Association (site built by Code for Boston)
waters_covered: Lower Charles River Basin, Watertown Dam to New Charles River Dam; 13 boathouses in 4 reaches
access_detail: Fetched: GET https://crwa-flagging.herokuapp.com/api/v1/boathouses (boathouse, latitude, longitude, reach, safe, overridden, reason); /api/v1/model (is_boating_season, model_outputs[reach, predictions[time, prediction, safe]], model_version, time_returned); /api/v1/model_input_data (rain, stream flow, gage height, air temp etc). No auth. Swagger docs linked from /api. Email alerts via CRWA; Twitter @crwaflagging.
cadence: Hourly model predictions in season (May to late October); off season the site shows no flags. Site banner seen today: 'The database has not updated in at least 24 hours.'
history: API returns 24 hourly predictions per reach; older history not exposed
license: API: 'CRWA allows open access to its Public Flagging API' (page wording). Code: MIT license (github.com/codeforboston/flagging).
status_reason: Open JSON API, good for the Charles River water page and a direct partner. Flag rules are public. Caveat: 'reason' still reads 'sewage' or 'cyanobacteria' while 'safe' is true off season, so read 'safe' plus is_boating_season, never 'reason' alone.
notes: Rules quoted: 'If any Combined Sewer Overflow (CSO) discharges took place in the past 48 hours in the Lower Basin, red flags will be flown downstream of the CSO discharge point.' Cyanobacteria: red 'for the duration of the bloom'. Flags: 'BLUE FLAGS mean the river is safe for recreation.' 'RED FLAGS mean there are public health risks.' 'Email communications from the CRWA are the official source for status updates.' 2025 Cambridge evaluation found flag programs 'well-supported by their recreational communities'.

name: Code for Boston 'flagging' open-source app (code behind the CRWA flag site)
access_detail: README fetched. Python/Flask app, Heroku deploy, demo mode with fake data, Alembic migrations, scheduled 'flask update-db'.
status_reason: Reusable reference for a staleness banner, a season switch, manual override with a reason, and a public API. It is an advisory app, not a discharge-event store.
notes: 14 forks; no evidence of deployment elsewhere.

name: Connecticut River Conservancy 'Is It Clean?' (isitclean.us)
operator: Connecticut River Conservancy (built with The Commons)
waters_covered: 250+ recreation sites on the Connecticut River and tributaries in four states
access_detail: Home and how-it-works pages fetched. Site data are embedded in Webflow CMS HTML; the page POSTs site lists to https://is-it-clean-089e6447542b.herokuapp.com/api/v1/weathers to get the 'likely condition'. No documented API or download. Results also go to EPA Water Quality Exchange (so WQP may carry them).
cadence: Weekly sampling May to October (Wednesday mornings at many sites); 'Results are posted to this site's map within 24 hours after the sample was taken.'
history: Since about 2012 (original 'Is It Clean' database); new site launched 26 Aug 2025
license: none stated beyond site privacy/terms link
status_reason: The bacteria source for the Connecticut River, the project's founding river. Partner first: ask CRC for a feed or a WQX pull, and reuse its 'latest sample' versus 'likely condition' split and recency legend.
notes: Categories: 'clean for swimming', 'clean for boating only', 'not clean for either'. Two layers: 'Latest samples: reflect the most recent water test results.' 'Likely condition: based on recent weather and historical trends.' Recency legend: less than a month / 1-12 months / more than 12 months. Disclaimer: 'While we can't guarantee water safety, we give you the tools to assess the risks yourself.' Tip: 'Avoid contact with the river downstream of a sewage outfall'. 2026 season funded by a $50,000 MassDEP grant.

name: Mystic River Watershed Association daily Boating Advisory (recflag API)
waters_covered: Mystic River at Rt 16, Malden River at Rt 16, Upper Mystic Lake (Shannon Beach)
access_detail: Fetched GET https://myrwa-api.org/api/recflag/predictions/ (no auth): per site {name, site{name, description, latitude, longitude}, current{timestamp, timestamp_local, prob, exceedance, predictors, flags, status{type,label,reason}}, history[7 days]}. Map script https://myrwa-api.org/api/recflag/static/map/build.js. Twitter @SafeMystic.

status.label: Good
status.reason: Low probability of elevated bacteria levels.

cadence: Daily prediction at about 5 AM, 'valid for the rest of the day'
status_reason: Small, clean JSON with explicit status types including 'unknown' and a plain-language reason. Ingestible for two Mystic waters; also a good status vocabulary.
notes: Status types: good / advisory / uncertain / unknown (CSS shows recflag-status-good/advisory/uncertain/unknown). Page definitions: Good (boating probably safe), Advisory (E. coli exceedances likely or bloom over state guideline), Uncertain (possible bloom), Not Available ('missing data or a system error'). Model built from 80 samples 2015-2016. CSOs are not a model input. MyRWA: 'In general MyRWA recommends not recreating on the water for 48 hours after heavy rainfall.' No Malden River slug in openboatlaunch.

name: MyRWA CSO pages and sign-up guide (Mystic, Alewife Brook, Chelsea Creek)
waters_covered: Mystic River, Alewife Brook, Chelsea Creek
access_detail: Fetched. Points readers to MWRA Everbridge sign-up (account required) and separate Boston, Cambridge, Chelsea and Somerville alerts; embeds a CSO outfall map; links the WBUR tracker.
status_reason: Shows the same fragmentation problem (four city channels plus MWRA for one river). Context, not data.
notes: Says 2023 CSOs into Mystic and Alewife Brook exceeded 200 million gallons; cites MA EEA data portal (data from mid-2022).

name: WBUR 'Map: Real-time sewage overflows into Mass. rivers and bays'
waters_covered: 180+ Massachusetts CSOs
access_detail: Page and https://api.wbur.org/pages?slug=combined-sewer-overflow-map&source=news fetched. The map is a Flourish embed; no data feed exposed.
cadence: Claimed: 'reflect a new alert within 10 minutes of an agency's alert'
status_reason: The closest earlier attempt at what DirtyWaterWatch plans for Massachusetts: it scraped agency alert emails and web pages into one 48-hour map. It is now broken. Its editor's note reads: 'This tracker appears to be malfunctioning and does not reflect the latest sewage overflow information.'
notes: 'This map is powered through online and/or email public alert systems.' 'WBUR is unable to independently verify the status of each CSO.' 'Use caution near waterways with CSO locations during and up to 48 hours after heavy rainfall.' The lesson is source-health monitoring and a visible stale-data state.

name: Cambridge MA CSO Real-Time, Onsite Notification System Evaluation Report (Kleinfelder, 29 Aug 2025)
waters_covered: Charles River, Alewife Brook
access_detail: Downloaded (16 MB, 256 pp) to scratchpad, text extracted; not kept in raw.
legal_basis: 2024 MassDEP/EPA water quality standards variance; 314 CMR 16.00
status_reason: The best US survey of on-site real-time CSO notification. It found only five such systems: DC Water, Lancaster PA and Chelsea MA beacon lights, and the ALCOSAN and CRWA flags. It also covers how the public received them.
notes: Findings: beacon systems drew 'limited to mixed feedback'; flagging systems were 'well-supported by their recreational communities'. Beacon cost about $15,660 each; seven Cambridge sites planned. Cambridge's process: flow-meter alarms, then staff verification, then website/email/sign within 4 hours; notices in 9 languages. Water quality buoys rejected (no bacteria sensing). Lists GLOWanus lanterns.

name: Massachusetts Rivers Alliance Sewage Right to Know campaign
access_detail: Fetched. Campaign history, law summary, town-by-town sign-up list, links to the MassDEP data portal https://eeaonline.eea.state.ma.us/portal/dep/cso-data-portal/
legal_basis: Chapter 322 of the Acts of 2020; 314 CMR 16.00
status_reason: Advocacy context and a likely partner. Its town-by-town sign-up list overlaps the MA state agent's discharger table.
notes: Law as summarised by the campaign: notification 'within 2 hours of discovering the discharge', 'updates every 8 hours while a discharge is occurring', warning signage. The campaign won full notification for 'blended sewage' in the final rules. Page undated (about 2022). Says 187 CSO outfalls and 19 permittees (MassDEP 2023 report says 194 outfalls).

name: Swim Guide (theswimguide.org and app)
operator: Swim Drink Fish Canada (with Waterkeeper Alliance affiliates)
waters_covered: 10,000+ locations; New England listings: MA 529, NH 178, RI 106, CT 77, ME 70, VT none (state listing pages, 2026-11-01)
access_detail: Fetched state pages and a beach page (/beach/3842). A Nuxt app; data appear in the server-rendered window.__NUXT__ payload. No public API documented. An open data standard for feeding results in exists (2017 announcement; copy at github.com/dylanneild/opendata).
cadence: Varies by affiliate. MA text: 'Swim Guide checks for the latest information daily, Monday - Friday during the swimming season.'
license: Legal page: trademarks 'licensed for non-commercial use to other organizations'; no data reuse terms found. 'Swim Guide shares the best information we have at the moment you ask for it.'
status_reason: Partner, not a feed. It is the biggest consumer-facing swim app. Its beach record design (separate result and posted dates, feed source health, thresholds, manual rating) is the closest schema to ours. DirtyWaterWatch could offer discharge events to it through its open data standard.
notes: MA beaches are assigned to 'The Swim Guide - Massachusetts' (Swim Drink Fish staff in Toronto transcribing DPH data), not to a local group. NE affiliates seen: NH Department of Environmental Services, Midcoast Conservancy (ME). Colour rules quoted for Provincetown: Green under 104 enterococci single sample or geomean of 5 under 35; Red above; 'Grey when there is no current or reliable monitoring information available.' Out of season everything shows 'No Data Available'.

name: Swim Drink Fish (Canada): Swim Guide operator, local hubs, Toronto sewage alert advocacy
access_detail: Blog posts found by search (Vancouver real-time spill alerts; 'A Model Sewage Alert System' for Toronto). Not fetched in depth.
status_reason: Operator context and Canadian advocacy for real-time sewage alerts. No data of its own for New England.

name: Surfrider Foundation Blue Water Task Force data portal
waters_covered: National; New England labs RI (URI; Narragansett Bay and south coast), NH (Seacoast), ME; no MA or CT rows in 2025 or 2026
access_detail: Fetched public CSV, no auth: https://mmvk4falrj.execute-api.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/v1/annual?year=2026 (all labs, one row per sample). The app itself uses an AWS AppSync GraphQL API (API key) at esvbxbhkmzgh5ojw3g2hvsx7du.appsync-api.us-west-2.amazonaws.com. Sample saved: raw/aggregators/bwtf-annual-2025-sample-ne.csv
cadence: Chapter dependent (weekly to monthly). Latest 2026 collection 2026-10-31, latest publication 2026-11-01T18:26Z. Lag can be long: one RI sample collected 2025-12-21 was published 2026-02-23.
history: Annual endpoint by year (2025: 10,186 rows nationally; 2026: 8,876 rows)
license: none found on portal (not checked beyond the app)
status_reason: Public machine-readable CSV with coordinates, collection time and publication time as separate fields. Covers Narragansett Bay sites near Providence CSOs (Fields Point, Bold Point Park, Gaspee Point, Stillhouse Cove, Rocky Point).
notes: 2026 New England rows: RI 211, NH 53, ME 9. Ask Surfrider for terms before ingesting. Field 'collection date' shows 'Invalid Date'; use 'stored collectionTime'.

name: EPA BEACON 2.0 (Beach Advisory and Closing On-line Notification) as a public product
waters_covered: Coastal and Great Lakes beaches of BEACH Act grantees, including all NE coastal states
access_detail: Map page and About page fetched (the sibling project could not reach it on 2026-10-18; it answered today). rss-page returns 'Application 132 Page rss-page not found'. Report wizard downloads not exercised.
cadence: Annual. About page: 'jurisdictions ... are not required to submit their beach season data to the EPA until the beginning of the following calendar year'
status_reason: Authoritative but a season late. Use it for history and context on beach pages, not for current status. Environment America's reports are built on it.
notes: Version 25.05.04.01, last updated June 22, 2026.

name: EPA How's My Waterway
access_detail: App bundle v2.19.0 fetched. The Swimming tab shows ATTAINS 'recreation_use' assessments ('Good', 'Impaired (Issues Identified)', 'Condition Unknown'). The current bundle has no BEACON or beach references. Data come from ATTAINS and WQP.
cadence: ATTAINS cycles (two-year assessments)
status_reason: Shows assessment status, not current conditions or discharge events. Use only as a deep link ('State water-quality report') as the sibling project already planned.
notes: Swimming blurb: 'EPA, states, and tribes monitor and assess water quality to keep you safe while swimming, wading, or boating.' Shows how a federal product avoids a same-day verdict.

name: Heal the Bay Beach Report Card with NowCast (California)
waters_covered: California and some Pacific coast beaches
access_detail: Fetched app bundle and GET https://admin.beachreportcard.org/api/locations (JSON, no auth; per location dry_grade, wet_grade, grade_updated, alerts, geo).
cadence: Weekly grades from county sampling; NowCast daily in summer at modelled beaches
status_reason: Out of region. A model for separate dry and wet weather grades and for a rain advisory with a fixed window.
notes: Rain Advisory wording: 'The beach is under advisory due to significant rainfall in the past 72 hours. ... it is advised to take caution or avoid swimming at this beach for 3 days after a rain event.' Closure: 'remains closed until the source has been identified by the local health agency, the spill ceases, and sampling results indicate compliance'. NowCast FAQ: models 'are also unable to predict acute pollution events like sewage and oil spills.'

name: USGS/EPA Great Lakes beach NowCast (Ohio Nowcast and related)
access_detail: Search only. USGS reports compare regression models with the 'persistence' method (yesterday's sample).
status_reason: Evidence for showing sample age and model output separately (see lit rows).

name: Water Reporter / The Commons (Chesapeake Commons) community monitoring platform
access_detail: Search only. App and data platform used by Waterkeepers (Save The Bay RI, Friends of Casco Bay). A beta API was mentioned in 2022. The Commons built the 2025 isitclean.us site.
status_reason: Platform behind several New England volunteer programs. Worth asking whether its API exposes bacteria results for RI and ME groups.

name: Just Sewage: Sewage Releases (iOS app, England)
access_detail: App Store listing fetched. Version 1.0 dated 2025-09-14. Map, recent overflow events, outfall history, EA bathing ratings.
status_reason: England only. It shows how cheap a consumer app becomes once a national open feed exists. The search found no US equivalent from 2024 to 2026.

name: NYC DEP Waterbody Advisory System (beta) and its JSON API
waters_covered: 45 NYC waterbodies other than beaches (Harlem, East, Hudson, Gowanus, Newtown Creek, Jamaica Bay, etc.)
access_detail: Fetched app https://nycwaterbodyadvisory.azurewebsites.net/ (Angular + ArcGIS JS 4.33). Its API, no auth: /api/profile (config; today show_advisories='wq', i.e. the public app shows the water-quality tab only); /api/advisory?advisoryType=cso|wq[&occurredOn=ISO] (returned [] today = no active advisories); /api/rainfall-samples?page=0&pageSize=96&sensorId=; /api/calendar (server time). Layers named in profile: waterbody_wq_advisory_staging and waterbody_csov2_advisory_staging on services.arcgis.com/at3rDjch5X7i9Bag.
cadence: Model runs on real-time rain gauges at the 14 treatment plants; layers edited today (2026-11-01 18:06-18:08 UTC)
history: occurredOn parameter suggests historical queries; not tested beyond one date
legal_basis: NYS ECL 17-0826-a (Sewage Pollution Right to Know) context; NYC LTCP commitments
status_reason: The best US example of an official affected-area polygon with an end time ('on advisory until ...') for non-beach waters. Out of region now; a candidate when the site covers New York.
notes: Page: system 'uses water quality models and real-time rainfall data to provide detailed advisory durations'; 10 years of hourly modelled bacteria; NYS primary/secondary contact criteria (enterococcus STV 130 / 266 cfu/100 mL). UI wording: 'On Advisory', 'No Advisory', 'on advisory until MMM dd, hh:mm a', 'N hours left'. CSO volume legend: 'No discharge', '<=5 MG' ... '>1,000 MG'. Sign-up via Notify NYC. Contact ltcp@dep.nyc.gov. Labelled beta.

name: NYC DEP CSO waterbody advisory ArcGIS layers (NYCWaterbodiesContaminationAdvisory45_View, cso_prd, csov2_prod, staging/dev siblings)
waters_covered: 45 NYC waterbody polygons
access_detail: Fetched layer JSON, counts and samples for NYCWaterbodiesContaminationAdvisory45_View (the sibling project's lead; data last edited 2025-07-09), cso_prd (2026-06-26) and csov2_prod (2026-11-01 18:06 UTC). The app's own config points at the *_staging layers. Samples in raw/us-cities/.
cannot_fill: clear active flag: Advisory=1 on 35 of 45 polygons while the app API listed no active advisories
cadence: csov2_prod and staging edited within minutes of the fetch
status_reason: Field meanings are undocumented. 'Advisory' does not match the app's active list, and 'Expires' holds a 0001-01-01 placeholder. Use the app API, which is the authority; treat these layers as geometry plus model parameters only.
notes: Activity classes seen: 'Boating' 21, 'Bathing and Boating' 14, 'Minimize Contact' 9, 'Boating and Limited Bathing' 1 (NYS classes I, SB, SC, SD). A per-waterbody rainfall-curve model (A-F coefficients and a rainfall threshold) is a concrete pattern for a modelled duration.

name: Notify NYC waterbody / CSO advisories
access_detail: Not subscribed (brief rule). 2012 coverage says Notify NYC announces advisories during and after rain events for waterbodies on the DEP advisory page.
status_reason: Push channel; the owner can subscribe if NY is added.

name: GLOWanus storefront lanterns (Gowanus Canal CSO advisory lights)
operator: Van Alen Institute with Gowanus residents
access_detail: Fetched. Lanterns cycle colours 'when the Canal is under a City-issued waterbody advisory'; open-source code by Stuart Lynn.
status_reason: Shows that the NYC advisory state can drive physical displays. Displays ran 2023-2024; current status unclear.

name: Open Sewer Atlas NYC
access_detail: Search only. Community maps of sewersheds and CSO outfall drainage areas built from Open Data and data scraped from DEP publications (started 2013).
status_reason: Shows CSO drainage areas (sewersheds) as context, which is useful when a page explains why a CSO happened. No event data.

name: Riverkeeper (Hudson) Water Quality Portal
waters_covered: Hudson River watershed, sampling since 2008
access_detail: Portal home fetched (Mapbox + Sanity CMS); data endpoint not identified.
status_reason: Out of region; a model for a long-running sample history per point. Riverkeeper led the NY Sewage Pollution Right to Know Act.

name: Save the Sound Long Island Sound Beach Report and Sound Health Explorer
waters_covered: 192 Long Island Sound beaches (CT and NY)
access_detail: Sound Health Explorer home and 2026 press release fetched; underlying data come from health departments via the EPA Water Quality Portal.
cadence: Annual grades (2025 season released 19 May 2026); biennial full report (next spring 2027)
history: Grades and sample results back to 2003 for most beaches
status_reason: Annual grades give context for CT beach pages; WQP is the machine path.
notes: Only beaches 'sampled at least nine times' are graded; 77% A or B in 2025; 17.7% of wet-weather samples failed (wet = at least 0.25 in of rain in prior 48 h). The press release does not mention CSOs.

name: King County / Seattle Public Utilities real-time CSO status map and CSV feed
operator: King County Wastewater Treatment Division and Seattle Public Utilities
waters_covered: About 125 CSO outfalls in Seattle (King County and SPU)
access_detail: Fetched CSV https://your.kingcounty.gov/dnrp/library/wastewater/cso/img/CSO_metadata.CSV (Last-Modified 2026-11-01 18:20 GMT), used by ArcGIS web map 6de3cae45d914326a32ed120b5ace4f8 (refreshInterval 5 min). Old page aqua.kingcounty.gov embeds mapitpk.com, which no longer resolves.
cadence: Page: 'updated every 10 minutes'. DateTime is the feed generation time, identical on every row.
history: None in feed; confirmed data in monthly and annual reports to Washington Ecology
license: Web map item links King County GIS terms (https://kingcounty.gov/en/dept/kcit/data-information-services/gis-center/about/terms-conditions-copyrights); not read
status_reason: The simplest real-time outfall status feed found: a public CSV with four plain states. Candidate for the national phase and a model for our outfall status vocabulary.
notes: States and labels from the map renderer: CurrentlyOverflowing 'Overflowing now'; OverflowLast48hrs 'Overflowed in the last 48 hrs'; NoRecentOverflow 'No recent overflow'; NoData 'Data not available'. Today: 5 real outfalls in last 48 h, 11 NoData. Four 'Dummy' rows at lon -120 exist only to drive the legend; filter them out. Advice: 'Stay out of the water near combined sewer overflow outfalls for 48 hours after a combined sewer overflow occurs'. Caveat: 'the real-time data has not yet been reviewed for accuracy.'

name: ALCOSAN Sewer Overflow Advisories (SOAK) and CSO Flag Alert Program
waters_covered: Allegheny, Monongahela and Ohio Rivers (Pittsburgh); 9 flag sites
access_detail: Fetched page with advisory log (In / Out / Dry timestamps). Sign-up via Everbridge https://member.everbridge.net/index/337966681555020#/signup . Annual PDFs from 2014 plus a 1995-2013 summary.
cadence: April 1 to October 31, 8 a.m. to 7 p.m.; changes outside those hours are reported at 8 a.m. next day
history: Online log plus annual PDFs to 1995
legal_basis: ALCOSAN consent decree / CSO public notification
status_reason: Best three-state wording found. It separates 'happening' from 'ended but still impaired' from 'cleared'.
notes: Wording: 'Overflows are in effect; Minimize contact with waterways' / 'Overflows have ceased; Waterways may still be impaired.' / 'System is in dry weather operation; No advisories are in effect'. Orange 'C-S-O' flags lowered after 48 h without overflow. Conflict: Allegheny County Health Department FAQ says alerts are 'usually canceled 24 to 36 hours after sewer overflows end' and gives a May 1 season start, so two agencies give the same public different rules.

name: Allegheny County Health Department CSO Advisory FAQ
access_detail: Fetched.
status_reason: Shows public health framing: an advisory 'does not prohibit nor discourage' recreation; 'it's best to try and minimize contact'.
notes: Alerts last 1 to 45 days, average about seven; vulnerable groups named (weakened immune system, open cuts).

name: Three Rivers Waterkeeper (Pittsburgh) sampling posted to Swim Guide
access_detail: Search only. Weekly E. coli sampling posted to Swim Guide (one listing sampled 2026-07-09, posted 2026-07-10). No river flag system of its own was found; the flags are ALCOSAN's.
status_reason: Out of region. It is an example of a Waterkeeper using Swim Guide as its publishing channel.

name: MWRD (Chicago) CSO notifications, CSO map and Overflow Action Day alerts
operator: Metropolitan Water Reclamation District of Greater Chicago
access_detail: Page fetched. Email/SMS via Smart911 https://www.smart911.com/smart911/ref/reg.action?pa=mwrdcso ; map at https://geohub.mwrd.org/pages/cso (did not render; no CSO layer found via GeoHub search).
cadence: A secondhand plan (Evanston) describes the map as updated daily
status_reason: Two lessons. Moving to a new alert platform on 17 June 2025 forced every subscriber to re-register. And 'Overflow Action Day' alerts ask people to use less water; they are not recreation advisories, so the two must not be mixed up.
notes: Friends of the Chicago River: one CSO in the Chicago-Calumet system in 2024. The City of Chicago planned a pilot of beacon lights (red during, yellow after) at four sites (River Park, Clark Park, Ping Tom Park, Park 571); its status after 2025 was not confirmed.

name: Friends of the Chicago River (Overflow Action Days, city notification pilot advocacy)
access_detail: Fetched two posts (April and June 2025).
status_reason: Advocacy that got CSO notification into the City of Chicago's 2024 IEPA permit; pilot design used paddler input (45+ participants).

name: Milwaukee MMSD overflow notices and Water Drop Alerts
access_detail: Search only. News posts per event with a map link and the '5-day letter' to Wisconsin DNR; Water Drop Alert texts ask people to use less water.
status_reason: A per-event news post is the publication channel; no feed found.

name: Michigan EGLE MiEnviro Portal public CSO/SSO/RTB discharge list (JSON behind the search page)
operator: Michigan Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy
waters_covered: Statewide; named receiving water per report
access_detail: Fetched (no login): GET https://mienviro.michigan.gov/ncore/ss/ssolist?includeMetadataInResponse=false&loadChildren=false&queryParams={"filter":[{"eventStartDateMin":"2026-10-01"}],"top":5} returns gzip JSON {queryResults[...]}; lookups at /ncore/ss/ssolistlookups (12,752 receiving waters, 92 counties, statuses COMPLETE/IN_PROCESS). Filters: reportStatusId, responsiblePartyName, siteName, permitNumber, eventStartDateMin/Max, eventEndDateMin/Max, receivingWater, counties, submissionReferenceNumber. The UI has a CSV download and public email subscriptions by county/township.
cadence: As filed by permittees; Michigan rule requires notice within 24 hours (not quoted here, state law outside this area). Sample: event 2026-10-01 23:20, report received 2026-10-02 00:40.
history: Annual reports since July 2000 (PDF); MiEnviro list depth not measured
legal_basis: MCL 324.3112a (Part 31, NREPA); 40 CFR 122.38 for Great Lakes CSOs
status_reason: The richest statewide discharge record found in the US: initial versus final status, start and end, quality, volume, receiving water and permit, all in public JSON. The model for our event schema and for any state agency we ask to publish. Candidate feed for national expansion.
notes: Start and end are equal on many initial reports (end not yet known); treat end_at as unknown until status is COMPLETE. Values are doubled strings ('CSO Discharge,CSO Discharge') because of multi-section forms. The API is undocumented and may change.

name: Federal Great Lakes CSO public notification rule, 40 CFR 122.38 (2018)
access_detail: eCFR redirected to an unblock page; text read on LII.
status_reason: Sets the content of a CSO notice (waterbody, location, public access areas affected, start, continuing or ended, end time, volume within 7 days). Use it as the minimum checklist of fields for our event record. It does not apply to New England.
notes: Initial notice 'As soon as possible, but no later than four (4) hours' after becoming aware; public notice must be electronic; supplemental notice 'Within seven (7) days' with volume and end time; annual notice 'by May 1'; recipients include local public health department and 'Indian Tribes whose waters may be impacted'. Signs must stay 'legible, visible and factually correct.'

name: Ohio Lake Erie CSO notification (NEORSD Edgewater advisories, Euclid, Lakewood)
access_detail: Search only. Euclid reports from monitoring at 17 CSO sites; NEORSD posts beach advisories (Edgewater) after CSOs. The Lakewood real-time site listed by EPA (cso.lakewoodoh.gov) does not resolve (DNS ENOTFOUND).
status_reason: Shows what the Great Lakes rule produced: one page per city and no state aggregation. PIRG criticises Ohio EPA enforcement.

name: Lakewood OH CSO real-time notification site (listed on EPA's real-time page)
access_detail: WebFetch: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND.
status_reason: Host does not resolve, yet EPA still links it (page updated 2026-03-09). Link rot is a risk for any list of notification channels.

name: Columbus OH Sewer Overflow Discharge Information (SSOCSO) dashboard
access_detail: ArcGIS item metadata fetched (modified 2024-04-23); layers not probed.
status_reason: Another ArcGIS dashboard pattern; national phase only.

name: Indiana IDEM CSO public notification rule (327 IAC 5-2.1) and statewide CSO outfall map
access_detail: ArcGIS web map item b089af99f7cd432cb94cdad4fbe14053 metadata fetched (every active and inactive CSO with NPDES number, CSO number, receiving stream, status; modified 2025-01-02). Rule text via search results only.
legal_basis: 327 IAC 5-2.1 (e.g. 5-2.1-6 community notification methods: annual March newspaper notice inviting requests)
status_reason: A statewide outfall map like the ones our state agents need. Notices themselves stay with each community.

name: Citizens Energy Group (Indianapolis) forecast-based CSO warnings
access_detail: Fetched blog post.
status_reason: A forecast-triggered warning: email goes out when the forecast calls for about a quarter inch of rain, before any overflow is measured. It shows the difference between forecast, observed and modelled advisories, which our labels must keep apart.
notes: Advice: 'avoid all contact with waterways downstream in the CSO areas (listed in the email) for four days.' Mandated by the EPA consent decree.

name: Wisconsin DNR sanitary sewer overflow reporting (Form 3400-184)
access_detail: Fetched. Reports go to DNR through the Switchboard portal 'within 5 business days of the event'; the page names no public list, map or download.
legal_basis: s. NR 210.21(4)(b), Wis. Adm. Code; WPDES permit standard conditions
status_reason: No public database found; agency-only reporting.

name: DC Water combined sewer system pages and CSO beacon lights
access_detail: Page fetched (redirects to /about-dc-water/what-we-do/wastewater-collection/css). It embeds a 2017 sewershed web app (item 7796821c5b6a4166b4eae7f17d915a78). No real-time status or alert sign-up found on the page, although EPA lists DC as having real-time notification and the Cambridge report describes DC Water beacon lights.
status_reason: Real-time channel not located: 48 potentially active outfalls, signs at each outfall. Needs another look if DC is ever in scope.
notes: Page wording: 'Avoid Contact with Combined Sewer Overflows'.

name: Anacostia Riverkeeper water quality monitoring (posted to Swim Guide)
access_detail: Search only (Swim Guide listings). Weekly or biweekly May 1 to Sept 15; green under 126 MPN E. coli.
status_reason: Shows one way to handle a legal swim ban: a note on listings says that even 'green' sites are under a 'DISTRICT-WIDE SWIM BAN' ... 'do NOT swim there'. The ban overrides the sample colour.
notes: Rule cited: no swimming for 48 hours after 0.5 in or more of rain.

name: Portland (OR) BES CSO advisories
waters_covered: Willamette River, Columbia Slough
access_detail: Fetched. GovDelivery email list https://public.govdelivery.com/accounts/ORPORTLAND_ENT/signup/39493 ; each event is a news post ('CSO advisory: heavy rain leads to combined sewer overflow to Willamette River'); page table lists 50 events 2012 to March 2026.
status_reason: A rare-event model (about four a rainy season since the Big Pipe): a news post plus an email list is enough at that frequency.
notes: Advice: 'stay out of the water for 48 hours following a CSO.'

name: Philadelphia Water Department CSOcast
waters_covered: 164 CSO outfalls (Delaware, Schuylkill, Cobbs, Tacony, Pennypack, etc.)
access_detail: Fetched FeatureServer https://services2.arcgis.com/POWz8dBwmjnei8fu/ArcGIS/rest/services/CSOCast_Layerboard/FeatureServer/0 (outfall status) and /1 (rain gauges); production web map 7f85bb92f6884cefa687226ba96684f3. Data last edited 2026-11-01 17:50 UTC.

sample_record.Name: C_01
sample_record.Status_Message: No overflow in the past 72 hours.
sample_record.Street: City Line Ave and Haveford Ave

cadence: Per-outfall poll times; SWMM model plus flow monitors
status_reason: A per-outfall 'last poll' time is the right pattern. But today 72 of 164 outfalls (44%) read 'Data is not currently available.', and PWD says CSOcast 'is not intended to be used as a water quality notification system for recreation.'
notes: Domain values: 'No overflow in the past 24 hours.', 'Overflow in the past 24 hours.', 'Currently overflowing.', 'Data is not currently available.'; live rows use 'No overflow in the past 72 hours.', so the domain and data disagree. Page: overflowing waterways 'may remain unsafe for recreation for a period of up to 72 hours following storm events'. Disclaimer: 'some monitors may occasionally report inaccurate information and sometimes no information at all.'

name: City of Erie (PA) Bureau of Sewers CSO Monitoring map
access_detail: Fetched; statuses render client-side; daily, 7-day and annual report links. Built by Process and Data Automation, LLC.
status_reason: A vendor-hosted map (Telog) of the kind many small utilities buy; no open feed seen.

name: New Jersey CSO notification systems (North Hudson Waterbody Advisory System, PVSC, Camden CCMUA, Trenton)
access_detail: Search only. NHSA has a sensor-based colour map with last-event end times; CCMUA shows outfall 'CLOSED' condition; NJDEP has a CSO outfall GIS layer with a status field (mapsdep.nj.gov Features/Utilities/MapServer/0).
status_reason: Neighbouring-state examples; NY Baykeeper criticised the joint site for highlighting municipalities 'when it rains' rather than actual discharges.

name: EPA 'Combined Sewer Overflow Real-Time Notification' page (list of community systems)
access_detail: Fetched (updated 2026-03-09). Lists DC Water, Mishawaka IN, MWRA, NYC, Lakewood OH, Portland OR, ALCOSAN, Erie PA, Philadelphia, King County, Spokane.
status_reason: Useful index of US real-time systems. It gives no guidance on what a notice should contain, and at least one link (Lakewood) is dead.
notes: Spokane (https://my.spokanecity.org/publicworks/wastewater/cso/) and Mishawaka (https://mishawaka.in.gov/.../cso-information/) not opened.

name: Surfers Against Sewage Safer Seas and Rivers Service (app and map)
waters_covered: Bathing waters and some river spots in England, Wales; 48 of 89 Scottish bathing waters since Sept 2025
access_detail: sas.org.uk answers 403 to scripted fetches. Facts from SAS Data HQ article (4 June 2026, fetched) and press. No public API found.
status_reason: The most-used sewage alert app. Its key lesson is governance: SAS 'does not set the rules for how individual sewage discharges get turned into bathing water alerts'. Each water company's own model decides, so the same red cross means different things by region.
notes: Display: 'a red cross or a green tick'. Inputs combine pollution risk forecasts, sewage alerts from company EDM feeds, and confirmed incidents. Scotland trigger: discharge 'within 2km' of a bathing site; 'will not confirm whether it is safe to swim'. From June 2026 SAS switched to Southern Water's modelled alerts after years of using its own precautionary rule, giving fewer alerts that SAS says are more accurate but 'not yet good enough'. Persistence window after a spill ends was not confirmed. Users can email their MSP from an alert.

name: SAS Sewage Data HQ (live UK sewage map)
access_detail: Data investigations page fetched; map uses the National Storm Overflow Hub API (per Water UK coverage).
status_reason: An advocacy view of the national feed.

name: Water UK National Storm Overflow Hub / Stream storm overflow activity feeds (England)
operator: Water UK and Stream (water company open data collaboration)
waters_covered: About 14,000 storm overflows in England
access_detail: Fetched Thames Water's layer (one of the per-company Stream feature services): https://services2.arcgis.com/g6o32ZDQ33GpCIu3/arcgis/rest/services/Thames_Water_Storm_Overflow_Activity_(Production)_view/FeatureServer/0 (573 overflows; data edited 2026-11-01 18:34 UTC). Same schema items found for Severn Trent, United Utilities, Northumbrian, Anglian, Yorkshire, South West, Wessex, and a Scottish Water copy. Water UK hub pages answer 403 to scripts.
cadence: Thames: 'refreshed at intervals of 5 minutes'; statute requires publication within one hour of start and of end
history: Current state plus latest event only; Thames has a separate historical alerts API
legal_basis: Water Industry Act 1991 s.141DA (inserted by Environment Act 2021 s.81)
status_reason: The reference schema for an outfall status record: one row per overflow, an explicit offline state, status start time, latest event start and end, receiving water and last-updated time, under an open licence. Copy it for DirtyWaterWatch's outfall table.
notes: Status values seen: -1 (34 overflows; offline/monitor not reporting, inferred from Top of the Poops 'Offline' column), 0 (538, not discharging), 1 (1, discharging). Thames: 'The data is not validated at the point when it is published because we want to be transparent and alert the public to potential issues as quickly as possible.'

name: Water Industry Act 1991 s.141DA: duty to publish near real-time storm overflow information
access_detail: Fetched.
legal_basis: Water Industry Act 1991 s.141DA (Environment Act 2021 s.81); in force 17 May 2024 for specified purposes and 1 January 2025 otherwise
status_reason: A statute that requires machine-timely publication: that a discharge occurred, where, start time within an hour, end time within an hour, 'in a form which allows the public readily to understand it'. It is a benchmark when comparing New England laws (MA: 2 hours plus 8-hour updates).

name: Southern Water Beachbuoy
access_detail: 403 to WebFetch. Facts from Ford et al. 2025 (abstract fetched) and SAS (June 2026).
status_reason: A warning about modelled impact labels. Since April 2022 releases are split into 'genuine', 'genuine but non-impacting' and 'not genuine'. Researchers found 19% of genuine discharge minutes were labelled non-impacting, often across several tide cycles, and some monitors gave false alarms 100% of the time.

name: The Rivers Trust Sewage Map
access_detail: 403 to WebFetch. ArcGIS org services3.arcgis.com/Bb8lfThdhugyc4G3 hosts annual EDM layers (2018/19, 2020) and a Scottish Water activity copy (found via ArcGIS search, not queried). Uses the National Hub API per Water UK.
status_reason: Combines annual totals with live status; not reached directly.

name: Top of the Poops (live map /now and annual league tables)
access_detail: Fetched. Counts per company: Overflowing (57 nationally), Offline (416), Not Overflowing, 'Overflowed since yesterday' (180).
license: '© 2020-2025 Top-Of-The-Poops CC-BY-SA 4.0'; Water UK data CC-BY-SA 4.0; asks visitors not to scrape
status_reason: Puts offline monitors in their own column (Yorkshire alone has 241). It also documents a fix we need: companies send several 'Started' signals for one event, so it keeps the earliest plausible start.

name: SewageMap.co.uk and POOPy (downstream-of-spill map and open-source EDM toolkit)
access_detail: Site shell fetched; POOPy README fetched (https://github.com/AlexLipp/POOPy); EGU26-7995 abstract fetched.
status_reason: The closest product to a 'modeled reach' layer. It traces river sections downstream of spills in the last 48 hours on a hydrological network. About 80% of users are on phones, 300,000+ visitors in a year, and its embeddable maps are used by news outlets.
notes: The 48-hour downstream method is not documented in the README. The GPL licence matters if code is reused.

name: Environment Agency Bathing Water Quality API and Pollution Risk Forecasts (Swimfo)
access_detail: environment.data.gov.uk answered 403 (Azure gateway) to curl and WebFetch. Facts from councils and EA blog via search.
status_reason: Blocked from this machine. Search shows daily forecasts May to September for a subset of bathing waters, with 'advice against bathing' when a short-term pollution risk is forecast.
notes: Pollution risk defined as a short-term reduction lasting less than 72 hours; only 61 of 150 Devon and Cornwall bathing waters are in the forecast system.

name: Other UK company storm overflow maps (Welsh Water, South West Water WaterFit Live, Wessex, Yorkshire, Anglian, United Utilities, Severn Trent, Northumbrian, Scottish Water)
access_detail: ArcGIS item search lists each company's 'Storm Overflow Activity' feature service (same Stream schema); not individually queried. Scottish Water's open data help page did not resolve (appgateway-north.scottishwater.co.uk ENOTFOUND).
status_reason: Same schema as the Thames row; nothing extra for us.

name: beaches.ie (EPA Ireland bathing water information)
operator: Environmental Protection Agency (Ireland) with local authorities
access_detail: Home page fetched; notice categories and data access not on the home page.
status_reason: Off season it says so plainly ('The 2026 bathing season is closed. Out of season results are currently voluntarily reported by some local authorities.'). That is a good way to word a seasonal programme being inactive.

name: Metro Vancouver real-time sewer overflow map
access_detail: Search only. Shows overflows in progress and in the last 48 hours; warns errors may occur from 'instrument malfunctions or power outages'.
status_reason: Same 'now / last 48 hours' pattern; no feed found.

name: Other Canadian municipal CSO notification (Ottawa, Hamilton, Kingston, Winnipeg, Toronto)
access_detail: Search only. Hamilton has a live bypass and overflow map; Kingston shows overflows now or in the past 48 hours; Ottawa sources conflict on live reporting; Winnipeg ran a web 'present status' indicator pilot in 2004.
status_reason: Not researched in depth; recorded for completeness.

name: Environment and Climate Change Canada CSO points map service (annual counts by wastewater system)
access_detail: Service JSON fetched: annual layers 2016-2021 of 'number of CSO points that discharged' per system.
status_reason: Annual national statistics only, no events; outside the region.

name: Beachwatch NSW daily pollution forecasts and public GeoJSON
operator: NSW Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
waters_covered: 246 NSW swim sites
access_detail: Fetched GET https://api.beachwatch.nsw.gov.au/public/sites/geojson (no auth): per site pollutionForecast, pollutionForecastTimeStamp, latestResult, latestResultRating, latestResultObservationDate.
status_reason: The cleanest public record that keeps the forecast and the last sample separate, each with its own time stamp, and says 'Forecast not available' when there is none.
notes: Today: Unlikely 144, Possible 16, Forecast not available 86; latest results Good 197, Fair 31, Poor 13, Bad 5. Some 'latest results' are from February-March 2026, yet still shown as 'Good' beside today's forecast. Wording from press: 'Pollution is likely. Avoid swimming today.'

name: EPA Victoria Beach Report and Yarra Watch forecasts
access_detail: Search only. Forecasts Good / Fair / Poor, issued 10 am and 3 pm; next-day forecast covers midnight to midnight; SMS when a nearby beach is forecast Poor; 36 bay beaches and 4 Yarra sites.
status_reason: Shows forecasts with a fixed validity window and an SMS that fires only on 'Poor'.

name: Safeswim (Auckland and other NZ councils)
operator: Auckland Council / Watercare and partner councils
access_detail: Home page fetched (pin wording); FAQ answers via search. No public API found.
status_reason: The best rule found for turning a sensor overflow into an advisory: a network sensor overrides the model with a black 'Do not swim' pin for a fixed 48 hours. 52 overflow sensors are linked to 41 beaches, and pins are 'updated every 15 minutes'.
notes: Pins: 'Suitable for swimming', 'Swimming not advised', long-term red 'Swimming not advised', 'Do not swim' (black), 'Exercise caution'. FAQ (search): 'When a sensor detects an overflow in progress, the Safeswim system automatically overrides the model results at the associated beach with a temporary black pin for 48 hours.' Manual black pins stay until the issue is resolved.

name: LAWA 'Can I swim here?' (New Zealand)
access_detail: Search only. Traffic-light grading (green suitable, amber caution, red not advised) of monitoring and predictive results for 1,000+ sites.
status_reason: National aggregation of council data, a model for a federated design.

name: Environment America Research & Policy Center / Frontier Group 'Safe for Swimming?' beach reports
operator: Environment America Research & Policy Center, Frontier Group, US PIRG
access_detail: environmentamerica.org answered 403 to WebFetch; facts from search snippets.
status_reason: An annual report built on BEACON data that uses 'potentially unsafe' days (the EPA Beach Action Value). It is a good model of careful wording, but a year late.
notes: Massachusetts: '47 Massachusetts coastal beaches were potentially unsafe for swimming on at least one quarter of days tested' in 2024 (search snippet). Year of other state figures unverified.

name: NRDC 'Testing the Waters' annual beach report (to 2014)
access_detail: Search only. 24th and apparently last edition released 25 June 2014 ('superstar' and 'repeat offender' beaches, about 3,500 testing locations); 2013 used five-star ratings.
status_reason: Historical; no successor found. Why it ended was not found.

name: American Rivers (Most Endangered Rivers, sewage and CSO advocacy)
access_detail: Search did not confirm any Most Endangered listing of the Merrimack or Connecticut for CSOs.
status_reason: Context only; no data product.

name: Waterkeeper Alliance (Swim Guide partner, Water Reporter partner)
access_detail: Search only. Member groups have published through Swim Guide since about 2012; Water Reporter was built with the Alliance.
status_reason: A network route to New England Waterkeepers; no sewage data product of its own found.

name: Sewage Overflow Community Right-to-Know Act (federal bill, several Congresses)
access_detail: S.396 (113th) text fetched. Earlier versions: H.R.2215 (108th), S.2080 and H.R.2452 (110th), H.R.753 and S.937 (111th), S.3388 (112th). Never enacted as found. A 2021 Trahan-LaHood bill and a Moulton 'Stop CSO Act' appear in search results.
status_reason: Never passed. Its 24-hour public notice standard is weaker than the Massachusetts and UK rules.
notes: S.396: notify the public 'as soon as practicable but not later than 24 hours after the time the owner or operator knows of the overflow'; immediate notice to health authorities when an overflow 'may imminently and substantially endanger human health'; requires 'a feasible methodology, technology, or management program for monitoring sewer overflows'.

name: EPA National Beach Guidance (2014) and 1994 CSO Control Policy public notification minimum control
access_detail: Not fetched in this pass (science and federal agents likely cover). The 1994 policy's nine minimum controls include public notification.
status_reason: Wording guidance to quote; not verified here.

name: Beachgoers' responses to beach health advisories
operator: Jones J, Aslan A, Nazaruk D, Zeki S. 2024. Journal of Water and Health 22(3):565-571. doi:10.2166/wh.2024.306
access_detail: Jones J, Aslan A, Nazaruk D, Zeki S. 2024. Journal of Water and Health 22(3):565-571. doi:10.2166/wh.2024.306
status_reason: Of 238 Georgia beachgoers, 41.2% had never read a contamination sign and 36.1% did not know beaches are monitored. Just over half judged safety by look and smell. Most would still visit under an advisory but stay out of the water (visitors 40% would not come vs residents 13.4%).

name: Is the Public Aware of Water Quality Monitoring and Safety Notifications on Beaches? (Georgia)
operator: Journal of the Georgia Public Health Association, 2023 (vol 9 iss 1)
access_detail: Journal of the Georgia Public Health Association, 2023 (vol 9 iss 1)
status_reason: Same respondent pool: nearly two-thirds felt current signage was inadequate.

name: Warning signs at beaches: do they work?
operator: Matthews B, Andronaco R, Adams A. Safety Science (2014); 472 interviews at four Victorian beaches
access_detail: Matthews B, Andronaco R, Adams A. Safety Science (2014); 472 interviews at four Victorian beaches
status_reason: Under half (45%) of beach users reported seeing any signage; hazard symbols were noticed most. Signs alone reach a minority.

name: A comprehensive analysis of CSO discharges to coastal waters and data communications by a UK water company 2021-2023
operator: Ford A, Boakes R, Richardson J, Owens M. 2025. Environmental Science: Water Research & Technology. doi:10.1039/D4EW00693C
access_detail: Ford A, Boakes R, Richardson J, Owens M. 2025. Environmental Science: Water Research & Technology. doi:10.1039/D4EW00693C
status_reason: Beachbuoy labelled 19% of genuine discharge minutes 'non-impacting' even when discharges spanned several tides; false alarms varied widely by monitor; false negatives unknown. Calls for transparency of the models behind public alerts.

name: SewageMap.co.uk and POOPy: open-source tools for communicating sewage impacts in real time
operator: Lipp A, Dawe J. 2026. EGU General Assembly abstract EGU26-7995
access_detail: Lipp A, Dawe J. 2026. EGU General Assembly abstract EGU26-7995
status_reason: Linking live spill data to a hydrological model to flag downstream rivers was what swimmers, kayakers and rowers valued. 80% of use is mobile, and embeddable maps spread through news outlets.

name: USGS SIR 2013-5166: validation of beach predictive models against the persistence method
operator: Francy DS et al. 2013. USGS Scientific Investigations Report 2013-5166
access_detail: Francy DS et al. 2013. USGS Scientific Investigations Report 2013-5166
status_reason: Of 42 models, 24 gave overall correct responses at least 5% more often than using the previous day's sample; models beat persistence on sensitivity (17 vs 4 models meeting goals). A day-old sample is a weak proxy for today.

name: USGS OFR 2007-1427: Lake Erie beach models vs previous-day E. coli
access_detail: USGS Open-File Report 2007-1427
status_reason: Models were correct on 82.7% and 82.1% of days at two beaches, but only 61.3% at Villa Angela. Model value is site-specific.

name: Association between CSO events and gastrointestinal illness in Massachusetts municipalities, 2014-2019
operator: Haley et al. 2024. Environmental Health Perspectives doi:10.1289/EHP14213
access_detail: Haley et al. 2024. Environmental Health Perspectives doi:10.1289/EHP14213
status_reason: Emergency visits for GI illness rose 22% after large CSOs and 62% after very large ones, over about four days, in Merrimack communities regardless of drinking water source (press summaries).
notes: ehp.niehs.nih.gov did not resolve from this machine. The science agent owns health evidence.

name: Strategies to increase notification of CSOs in Massachusetts (WPI Boston Project Center)
operator: Worcester Polytechnic Institute student project, 2020-2021; surveys of 87 boards of health and 20 watershed/EJ groups
access_detail: Worcester Polytechnic Institute student project, 2020-2021; surveys of 87 boards of health and 20 watershed/EJ groups
status_reason: Boards of health were confused about required signage and the notification process; the authors recommended training. Agency comprehension is itself a weak link.

name: Citizens' perception of combined sewer overflow spills into bathing coastal areas (Badalona/Barcelona)
access_detail: 2021 (UPC repository recercat 2117/355899)
status_reason: Qualitative: poor communication about CSO spills led to misunderstanding and loss of trust in the city council.

name: City of Winnipeg 2004 CSO public notification web pilot report
operator: City of Winnipeg Water and Waste, 2004
access_detail: City of Winnipeg Water and Waste, 2004
status_reason: An early web 'present status' indicator dot. Its reach was measured only by page views; no user-comprehension evaluation.
